newsitem.title: UK: BP says Q1 1997 production at six-year high.
newsitem.headline: BP says Q1 1997 production at six-year high.

text.p: British Petroleum Plc (BP) said on Tuesday first quarter oil and gas production rose by 3.5 percent to a six-year high thanks to increased output from fields commissioned last year.

"The overall production level for the quarter was the highest for six years, with oil and gas production levels above those of a year ago by some three and six percent respectively," the company said in a statement.
Combined oil and gas output rose to 1.601 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from 1.546 million in the first quarter of 1996.

BP said the commissioning of the North Sea Harding and Andrew fields and the Mars field in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, together with strong gas sales in Britain, were largely responsible for the increase.

Despite a seasonal slowdown in the second quarter of 1997, BP said it expected annual production to be higher than in 1996, "reflecting a full year's contribution from the fields commissioned in 1996 and new production this year."
Earlier on Tuesday, a BP official said production at the company's troubled Foinaven field west of the Shetland Islands had been delayed again by bad weather.
An Aberdeen-based official said first oil was still "a few weeks" away.

Foinaven, the first field to be developed in the deep waters of the Atlantic margin, was originally due onstream in June 1996 but a series of technical mishaps and weather-related disruption has delayed the project by almost a year.
